clue.text: Reassess each asset, perhaps, depending on circumstances

indicators.note: to reassess is to assess over again, here taken as working the letters of the next two words afresh

parts.note: perhaps and maybe both express possibility

explanation.surface: An accountant revalues every holding, conditional on how things turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reassess' looks like the accountant's job but signals rearranging the two words after it; 'perhaps' then supplies the closing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means according to whichever situation actually applies, a synonym for depending on circumstances.

clue.text: Guess nocturnal spirits may be involved

definitions.meaning: a wild attempt made with no real knowledge, an idiomatic guess
read literally, a measure of whisky drunk after nightfall, spirits in the night

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a random attempt at an answer, and literally a dram of spirits taken in darkness.

clue.text: Topless 17 gives you the horn

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its first letter, its top in a down entry

parts.note: the answer to 17 across, a prostitute, gives the synonym strumpet

explanation.surface: A scantily clad prostitute hands over a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is HOOKER; a synonym is STRUMPET, and 'Topless' drops its initial S.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument is a kind of horn, the general name for lip-blown brass.

clue.text: Vile manager oppressing masses half-heartedly

indicators.note: in a down entry, the manager sits on top of the masses, pressing down on them

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a business manager

indicators.note: the word has a double-letter heart, and losing half of it leaves one B

parts.note: the rabble is the common masses, the mob

explanation.surface: A nasty boss bears down on the workers without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Bs of RABBLE, giving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is a straight synonym for vile: detestable, abominably bad.

clue.text: How one may sail, we hear, at rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb, shakes or upsets, so the letters before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: A sailor explains, by the sound of it, how to sail near rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound signal but is anagram fodder; 'rocks' shuffles WEHEAR plus AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for on or towards the windward side, a way one can sail a ship.

clue.text: Setter's come up with trick to use

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me; the 's stands for has
a ploy is a cunning trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler has devised a trick to exploit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reverses the setter's self-reference, read upwards in this down entry; 'use' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to work, to employ it, is to use it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Market oven guards alternatively

indicators.note: the cooker surrounds and protects the other piece, so it sits outside it

parts.note: an Aga is a British make of range cooker
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: At the market, a stove protects goods, or else.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British range cooker; 'guards' means the cooker surrounds the word for alternatively.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was the public square used as a marketplace.

clue.text: Partners first run going concerns

indicators.note: going means leaving, so a letter is taken out of the partners

parts.note: brothers can be partners in a firm, as in Warner Brothers

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run; first means the earlier of the two Rs

explanation.surface: In a firm, partners making a first run are going concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: BROTHERS has two Rs; 'first run going' removes the earlier one.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to concern someone is to worry or trouble them, which is a synonym.

clue.text: See criminal offer to enter one dodgy plea

indicators.note: the three pieces go into the scrambled letters, entering them
dodgy means unsound, so the letters of the word one are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a con is a convict, a criminal
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A lawyer notes a crook's offer to come in with one dubious plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' scrambles 'one', and 'to enter' places the three charade pieces inside it after its first two letters; the plea is legal Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for I do not wish to contend, a defendant's plea accepting conviction without admitting guilt.

clue.text: You reportedly squeezed into old trousers with retrograde look, as any homemaker should

indicators.note: with joins the second part on after the first
the letter is forced inside the garment, squeezed into it

parts.note: hose is an old word for breeches or tights

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word you is said aloud as the letter U

parts.note: said aloud, the word you sounds like a letter

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for a look is reversed

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Someone crams into old breeches with a backward glance, as every domestic should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the letter sounding like 'You'; 'squeezed into' puts it inside the old trousers, and 'retrograde' turns the word for look backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep house is to run a home, the job any homemaker should do.

clue.text: Bit of a lout, Donald Trump

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, a bit of them

explanation.surface: A thuggish lout, says someone, describing the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' takes the run spanning 'lout, Donald'. Trump here is a verb, not the president.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump someone is to beat or surpass them, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Lush plant once again turning westward

indicators.note: in an across entry, west is leftwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to repot is to plant again in a new pot

explanation.surface: A gardener's lush plant is moved again to face west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning westward' reverses REPOT. Lush is the slang noun for a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drinker, slang synonyms both for someone who drinks to excess.

clue.text: Decorator working in part of Paris

indicators.note: working means being worked on or shaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter-decorator is on the job in a Paris district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges DECORATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of Paris by the Seine, home to the Palais de Chaillot facing the Eiffel Tower.

clue.text: Celebs ill-equipped for dinner parties

definitions.meaning: lacking any furniture to eat at, as a phrase of two words

explanation.definitionFit: Notable people are distinguished figures, synonyms for celebrities; read as two words it means lacking furniture.

clue.text: CIA's involved in government department omnishambles

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in the department's abbreviation

parts.note: the FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the agency's initials with the s from the contraction kept

explanation.surface: The CIA meddles in a ministry's affairs, and chaos follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns CIAS into IASC, put 'in' FO, the British Foreign Office.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete and humiliating failure; omnishambles is modern British slang for a total mess.

clue.text: Like Iceland? It's gone bust

indicators.note: something that has gone bust is broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as the word it, with the 's standing for has

explanation.surface: A question about Iceland's banking collapse: the country has gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone bust' rearranges ICELAND plus IT. Iceland's banks collapsed in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Like as an adjective, meaning the same or alike, as in two like objects.

clue.text: Happen to find space traveller on French street

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a comet travels through space
rue is the French word for street

explanation.surface: Stumble across a heavenly body over a Paris boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue placement: the space traveller sits above the French street.
explanation.definitionFit: To come true is for a wish or prediction to happen, become reality: an idiom.

clue.text: Pro rugby player

definitions.meaning: the forward who hooks the ball in a rugby scrum

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a prostitute, and the name of a rugby forward position in the front row.

clue.text: Rank arrogance that's unacceptably forward

parts.note: rank as an adjective means rotten or off
side is an old word for swagger or pretension

explanation.surface: Plain arrogance makes for a pushy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE in the sense of airs or putting on side is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby, a player too far forward when the ball is played is penalised.

clue.text: Look of annoyance about team going over current failure

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a pout is a sulky look of annoyance

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A sulky expression greets the team crossing over after a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns CREW into WERC, which POUT goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure of the electricity supply; current refers to electric current.

clue.text: Killer's boxing clever, officer's found

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so the killer surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means quick to learn, clever

explanation.surface: A murderer is fighting a smart opponent, and the police have discovered him.
explanation.walkthrough: The first murderer of Genesis is the killer; 'boxing' wraps him round the word for clever, and 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of commanding officer in the army or navy, or the head of a ship.

clue.text: Asian said to get energy from this exercise?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for the Asian person is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand
chi is the vital energy in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Does an Asian person apparently draw vital force from this workout?
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes the Asian person's word heard, not spelt; chi is the Chinese life force the exercise is meant to channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese martial art practised as slow flowing exercise.

clue.text: Dog's back in English novelist's strip of greenery

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes in the novelist's name

parts.note: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe

indicators.note: back means read backwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A dog's rear end appears in an English author's description of a hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAIL into LIAT, put 'in' DEFOE. Strip is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip plants of their leaves; strip of greenery is a verb phrase meaning remove foliage.

clue.text: Fast, with zip? Au contraire!

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
zip means nothing, zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about speed and pep, answered with a firm denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclamation applied to 'Fast, with zip': the opposite, slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning slowly, the reverse of fast and lively, which is what Au contraire implies.

clue.text: Leg shown by model, a sitter

indicators.note: shown by puts the limb after the model in the answer

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
pin is slang for leg

explanation.surface: An artist's model sits for a portrait, showing a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A sitter in football is an easy goalscoring chance; 'shown by' places PIN after T and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a football sitter and a tap-in are goals so easy they can hardly be missed.

clue.text: What Beatrix of the Netherlands used to do in the shower, according to rumour

definitions.text: What Beatrix of the Netherlands used to do

indicators.note: rumour is what people say, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: what a shower does is rain

explanation.surface: Gossip about what the former Dutch queen got up to while bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: Beatrix was Queen of the Netherlands until 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch rules, governing as sovereign, which is what Queen Beatrix did until abdicating.

clue.text: Rail service repaired car with crack on the outside

indicators.note: the drug word goes outside the other letters

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine, coke
the RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: repaired means fixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A train company fixed a car that had a crack along its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: Rail here is the bird family, not the railway. 'repaired' scrambles 'car' after the navy abbreviation, and 'on the outside' wraps the drug round both.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of the rail family known for its rasping call in grassy fields.

clue.text: Vamp explored love in bed — not really fair!

indicators.note: to vamp is to revamp or improvise, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A seductress explored lovemaking in bed, and it was not fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vamp' rearranges EXPLORED, O, IN and BED; fair means blonde, here not naturally so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose fair hair comes from bleach is not naturally fair-haired.
